subject.title: [Bug]: Performance degradation in session memory sync: full delete-reinsert pattern for growing JSONL files

question: Should this be fixed as a fresh current-main incremental session indexing design, by rescuing the open candidate PR, or by intentionally retaining file-level rebuild with cache and batch mitigations?
rationale: The choice affects session-state correctness, memory_index schema behavior, source-wide batching, overlap semantics, and whether the open candidate branch is still worth adopting.

options.title: Fresh current-main fix
options.body: Implement incremental preservation against the current memory_index schema and batching paths, using the open PRs as context but not as the landing branch by default.

options.title: Rescue the open candidate PR
options.body: Ask the contributor or a maintainer to rebase https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/75179 and replace obsolete assumptions before further review.

options.title: Keep file-level rebuild
options.body: Close the direction only if maintainers decide embedding cache, delta thresholds, and full-entry consistency are preferable to incremental session indexing complexity.

recommendation.title: Fresh current-main fix
recommendation.body: Implement incremental preservation against the current memory_index schema and batching paths, using the open PRs as context but not as the landing branch by default.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory-core and memory-host-sdk storage/schema work makes this the best available routing candidate for the design choice.
